messages.subject: ezANOVA is adequate in this expt.?
parts:
Hi everyone,
I wonder if my experiment can be analyzed by using ezANOVA. I will try
to explain the experiment and variables & factors.

Individuals: A,B,C,D,E
Treatment: T1,T2
Time: 0, 24, 48, 72, 96
VD_Value: dependent variable

A treatment is applied to an individual, and it is measured 5 times
(in hours). The main goal is to know if there are significative
differences between Individuals (yes, also as treatments) and
Treatment (and their interactions) along the Time.
I think it is design of repeated measures or a mixed model, that can
be analyzed by using ez package. However, I can't figure how to design
such a model by using ezANOVA.
Thank you for your help.

messages.author: cb25d91fd630a4e5
messages.subject: Re: [ez4r] ezANOVA is adequate in this expt.?
parts:
If your data frame, "my_data", is set up with columns "Individual",
"Treatment", "Time", "VD_value", then you can run:

my_anova = ezANOVA(
data = my_data
, dv = .(VD_value)
, wid = .(Individual)
, within = .(Treatment,Time)
)
print(my_anova)

However, if you truly have only 5 individuals, you will likely receive
an error message after running the above which will suggest that you
add the "type=1" argument to the call to ezANOVA:

my_anova = ezANOVA(
data = my_data
, dv = .(VD_value)
, wid = .(Individual)
, within = .(Treatment,Time)
, type = 1
)
print(my_anova)

parts:
Ah, so you'd like to know whether there are differences between the
individuals? In that case, you should probably move to a mixed
modelling context:

#evaluate evidence for a difference between individual intercepts
my_data$dummy = factor(1) #create a dummy variable
restricted_model = lmer(
formula = VD_value ~ (1|dummy) #no individual differences
, data = my_data
)
unrestricted_model = lmer(
formula = VD_value ~ (1|Individual) #individual differences
, data = my_data
)
bits_of_evidence = (AIC(restricted)-AIC(unrestricted))*log2(exp(1))
print(bits_of_evidence)
# sign reflects whether the unrestricted (+) or restricted (-) model
is supported by the data
# magnitude reflects degree of support

#evaluate evidence for a difference between individual effects of Time
restricted_model = lmer(
formula = VD_value ~ (1|individual) + Time
, data = my_data
)
unrestricted_model = lmer(
formula = VD_value ~ (1+Time|Individual) + Time
, data = my_data
)
bits_of_evidence = (AIC(restricted)-AIC(unrestricted))*log2(exp(1))
print(bits_of_evidence)

#evaluate evidence for a difference between individual effects of Treatment
restricted_model = lmer(
formula = VD_value ~ (1|individual) + Treatment
, data = my_data
)
unrestricted_model = lmer(
formula = VD_value ~ (1+Treatment|Individual) + Treatment
, data = my_data
)
bits_of_evidence = (AIC(restricted)-AIC(unrestricted))*log2(exp(1))
print(bits_of_evidence)


#evaluate evidence for a difference between individual Time:Treatment
interactions
restricted_model = lmer(
formula = VD_value ~ (1+Time+Treatment|individual) +
Time+Treatment+Time:Treatment
, data = my_data
)
unrestricted_model = lmer(
formula = VD_value ~ (1+Time+Treatment+Time:Treatment|Individual)
+ Time+Treatment+Time:Treatment
, data = my_data
)
bits_of_evidence = (AIC(restricted)-AIC(unrestricted))*log2(exp(1))
print(bits_of_evidence)

ratios.
